chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Hasan al-Kinani, from Ja'far ibn Najih al-Kindi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ubaydullah al-Umari, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, God Mighty and Majestic sent down to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) a book before his passing. So he said: 'O Muhammad! This is your testament to the nobles from your family.' He said: 'And who are the nobles, O Jibril?' So he said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and his sons (peace be upon them).'

And upon the book there were seals of gold. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) handed it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and commanded him to break one seal from it and act according to what was in it. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) broke a seal and acted according to what was in it. Then he handed it to his son al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he broke a seal and acted according to what was in it.

Then he handed it to al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and he broke a seal and found in it: 'Go forth with a group of people toward martyrdom — there is no martyrdom for them except with you — and offer yourself for God Mighty and Majestic.' And he did so. Then he handed it to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and he broke a seal and found in it: 'Lower your head, be silent, stay in your home, and worship your Lord until certainty (death) comes to you.' And he did so.

Then he handed it to his son Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), and he broke a seal and found in it: 'Narrate to the people and issue verdicts for them, and do not fear anyone but God Mighty and Majestic, for there is no way for anyone against you.' And he did so. Then he handed it to his son Ja'far, and he broke a seal and found in it: 'Narrate to the people and issue verdicts for them, and spread the sciences of the People of your Household, and affirm your righteous forefathers, and do not fear anyone but God Mighty and Majestic — and you are in protection and security.' And he did so.
Then he handed it to his son Musa (peace be upon him), and likewise Musa will hand it to the one after him, and thus until the rise of al-Mahdi — may God's blessings be upon him.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةُ: Martyrdom — the divine command given to Imam al-Husayn to go forth with companions to martyrdom
key_terms.النُّجَبَةُ: The nobles/elite — Jibril identifies these as Ali ibn Abi Talib and his descendants
key_terms.الْيَقِينُ: Certainty — Quranic term (15:99) meaning death; Imam al-Sajjad commanded to worship until death
key_terms.حِرْزٌ وَأَمَانٌ: Protection and security — divine assurance given to Imam al-Sadiq
key_terms.خَوَاتِيمُ: Seals (plural of khatam) — gold seals on the divine book, each broken by the succeeding Imam
key_terms.قِيَامُ الْمَهْدِيِّ: The rise of al-Mahdi — the eschatological event marking the end of this chain of Imamate

ai.seo_question: What divine instructions did each Imam receive from the sealed book sent by God to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that God sent a sealed book to the Prophet Muhammad before his death, addressed to the noble members of his family — identified as Ali ibn Abi Talib and his descendants. Each Imam opened one seal and received divine instructions specific to his era and circumstances, from the command to seek martyrdom given to al-Husayn, to the injunction to stay silent given to Ali ibn al-Husayn, to the mandate to spread knowledge given to al-Baqir and al-Sadiq. The hadith establishes that each Imam's conduct was divinely ordained and not self-determined, reflecting the Shia theological doctrine that the Imams act only by divine command.
